::: {.project-meta}
**Status:** Complete; post-election scoring in progress | **Collaborators:** Team 5, UMass Amherst DACSS | **Methods:** Bayesian poll aggregation, Monte Carlo simulation, calibration on past midterms | **Tools:** Python, R | **Code:** public on GitHub
:::

Forecasts of the 2026 U.S. Senate and House elections, each run has 100,000 simulations that blend VoteHub polling, partisan-lean fundamentals, and Kalshi prediction-market prices. The Senate model was built with Team 5 in UMass Amherst's DACSS program, chosen from seven competing versions we built and tested against one another and calibrated against more than two decades of historical polling misses. I extended it on my own into a district-by-district House model covering all 435 seats, recalibrated on the 2018 and 2022 midterms. Both models ran on a schedule every three hours through the final week and made their last call at 9:00 AM on Election Day.
